title: Identifying through explicit identifier in registration
description: Government ID, name, and email are explicit identifiers collected during parent registration, directly revealing the identity of the data subject.

title: Sensitive data type collection
description: Government ID is a highly sensitive data type collected during registration, which may not be strictly required or could be minimized.
assumptions: Govt ID is included in the flow without specified necessity for auth.

title: Linking via unique identifier
description: Government ID serves as a unique identifier enabling linking of this registration data to the individual across contexts.
assumptions: Govt ID is unique and persistent.

title: Identifying through explicit identifier
description: Storing parent accounts in the MongoDB users collection likely involves explicit identifiers such as usernames, emails, or account IDs that directly reveal the parent's identity.
assumptions: Account storage typically requires at least one identifying attribute for authentication purposes.

title: Unique identifier linking
description: Parent account records are linked via unique identifiers stored in the users collection, enabling linkage of all related data to the specific parent account.
assumptions: Each parent account uses a unique key or ID in the database.

title: Excessive retention duration
description: Parent account data is retained in the datastore indefinitely or longer than necessary for authentication functionality.

title: Attributable persistent logging via account storage
description: Authentication service creates persistent attributable records of parent accounts that cannot be repudiated.

title: Unique identifier in JWT
